pr_comments: I think this PR could skip the news entry since this is just a refactoring change - or would this still need an entry?

This shouldn't have broken anything, but <strike> it looks like some seemingly unrelated things were passing in the useless `maxsize` argument: https://github.com/python/cpython/actions/runs/5845780591/job/15850226459?pr=107907#step:19:113</strike>
following the fixes for https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/107907#issuecomment-1676253988, this should start passing again since the failure was due to the inherited `LifoStack` still using expecting the `maxsize` argument in the overridden `_init` method.

<strike>Taking a look at https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3 to see if this can be updated - will post here again once that is resolved.</strike>

Update: it looks like the [failure I linked to above](https://github.com/python/cpython/actions/runs/5845780591/job/15850226459?pr=107907#step:19:113) wasn't actually a failure in the `urllib3` package, but a failure in the `queue.LifoStack` class that inherited from `queue.Queue`. Following the fixes in commit e5094abc692b27e9b90aa01727d7be6f87f331cb, this should start passing again since the failure was due to the inherited `LifoStack` still using expecting the `maxsize` argument in the overridden `_init` method.

inherited this `maxsize` argument and their corresponding <strike>tests</strike> `_init` methods also need to be updated (current failures: https://github.com/python/cpython/actions/runs/5845780591/job/15850226050?pr=107907#step:8:1056)

points to https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/ee40b3e20d9b8d62a9b36b777dff42db1e9049d5/Lib/queue.py#L34-L36

... but commits bacae73ca5e2f62694c1d2f7875ffc155035e651 and e5094abc692b27e9b90aa01727d7be6f87f331cb should address this. issue_context.title: Unused `maxsize` argument in `_init` method of `queue.Queue`
issue_context.body:
# Feature or enhancement

Note: this is less of a feature or enhancement, and more of a technical debt refactor - however, I don't see an Issue option for "Refactoring," so this is the closest label.

The `__init__` method of `queue.Queue` passes in the `maxsize` argument to the `_init` method:
https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/ee40b3e20d9b8d62a9b36b777dff42db1e9049d5/Lib/queue.py#L34-L36

but the `_init` method does not actually use the `maxsize` argument at all:
https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/ee40b3e20d9b8d62a9b36b777dff42db1e9049d5/Lib/queue.py#L205-L209

# Pitch

Remove this unused `maxsize` argument.



<!-- gh-linked-prs -->
### Linked PRs
* gh-107907
<!-- /gh-linked-prs -->
comments:
Also, it looks like `asyncio.queues.Queue` has some similar leftovers (https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/107907#issuecomment-1676265948):
https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/ee40b3e20d9b8d62a9b36b777dff42db1e9049d5/Lib/asyncio/queues.py#L33-L50

https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/ee40b3e20d9b8d62a9b36b777dff42db1e9049d5/Lib/asyncio/queues.py#L224-L227

https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/ee40b3e20d9b8d62a9b36b777dff42db1e9049d5/Lib/asyncio/queues.py#L237-L240

Since the Queue class is designed to be inherited from with `_init` overridden, I would suggest not to change this, especially when there is no tangible benefit beyond refactoring.

We wouldn't want to break user code that has its own `_init` implementation that expects `maxsize`, such as if someone has code like in https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/51586 that has been working for a decade.
That `maxsize` argument left unused for 10 years is also for compatibility reasons.

Interesting, I thought variables prefixed with a `_` (underscore) indicated that a variable/function/method is an "internal" implementation detail. Is that not the case for core modules? Or is that only for C source files for the core dependencies?

In that case, might it be useful to add a comment providing this context?

As noted by others, this would be a breaking change.  The code specifically advises users to override those methods in subclasses.  If you change the call signature, it breaks every one of those user customizations.  Also, some of the those may actually need the `maxsize` argument which is likely why Guido included it in the API.

There is also a principle of "Chesterson's fence" and an assumption that the people who came before you (the original author and all of the subsequent maintainers) knew what they were doing.

Got it, that makes sense - I know the `__init__` method is usually overridden in subclasses, but didn't see that the `_init` method here was supposed to be overridden in subclasses, and didn't see it in the [docs page either](https://docs.python.org/3/library/queue.html). Where is that written? (I understand this is a breaking change and won't go in, I'm just curious where this info was since I missed it)

Just to clarify - I thought this was keeping the API the same since the actual `queue.Queue` class initialization stayed the same (`__init__` still accepts the `maxsize` argument), and this change would only remove how the `maxsize` from being an "unused" variable in the `_init` method while `__init__` stayed the same.
